_comment: Interface texts of the English site, keyed as de.json (checks/test_site.py). British spelling with -ise; terms follow knowledge/glossary.md. `edition` holds the English form of the language-bound fields of edition/texts.json; `terms` translates labels the build coins itself (literal kinds, adjudication decisions, review stages, itinerary flags), while the act types and roles of the model come from the English prefLabels of the frozen vocabulary.

edition.title: Barbarossa Regesta
edition.subtitle: An experiment with LLM agents based on Regesta Imperii IV,2
edition.description: The edition adds to regesta of Frederick Barbarossa from Regesta Imperii a layer of statements, each bound to its wording in the regest and carrying a named producer and verification status. It is thus an assertive edition based on RI IV,2.
edition.licenceLine: Texts and data CC BY 4.0, code MIT. Regesta and index from Regesta Imperii Online (CC BY 4.0), modified.
edition.attribution: The regesta, commentaries and index entries on Frederick I Barbarossa come from Regesta Imperii, section IV,2 (RI IV,2,1–4 and index), edited by the German Commission for the Editing of the Regesta Imperii at the Academy of Sciences and Literature, Mainz, and available online in Regesta Imperii Online and as data in the RI Lab. They are licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International. The edition used a CSV export of the regesta and the index file RI_004-002-Barbarossa.csv, whose export date has yet to be established. The edition has modified the data. Markup was converted to plain text, regesta were selected and linked, and RDF statements were generated from the regest text with a Large Language Model (LLM). These statements, their verification status and the visualisations are results of this project and not statements of Regesta Imperii. The Academy of Sciences and Literature, Mainz, takes no part in the edition and has not reviewed it. Every regest links to its own page in Regesta Imperii Online.
edition.modification: Modified. Markup converted to plain text, regest selected and linked, statements generated from the regest text by LLM-based agents. The statements are not statements of Regesta Imperii.
edition.markNote: The mark of Digital Humanities Craft in the footer of the pages comes from the repository DigitalHumanitiesCraft/brand-assets (dhcraft-mark-watercolor-128.png). It is excluded from the licences of this edition and remains the property of Digital Humanities Craft OG.

ui.start.intro: The edition adds a layer of statements to the regesta of Frederick Barbarossa from Regesta Imperii. LLM agents derived the statements from the text of each regest, and every statement is bound to the wording it rests on. A regest is a calendar entry, a short summary of a charter or of an event, with its date, place and sources. Beside the statements stand all {n} regesta supplied by Regesta Imperii, with place and date.

ui.start.origin: The edition is a {promptotyping} experiment by {maker}, made as a teaching example for the guest unit {unit} on 20 November 2026 in the course “{course}” (graph-based systems) at the {university}. LLM agents in Claude Code generated the pipeline, the data and the interface. The idea of the space-time cube in the Atlas is taken from {windhager}, who describe the space-time cube for cultural heritage collection data. The agents worked with the AI harness of {maker}, that is, the instructions, working procedures and tools with which they are configured, and with its Obsidian vault. Both hold knowledge built up and curated over two years. A person sets the direction and assesses every intermediate state. So far no person has verified any statement of the edition against the sources.
ui.start.files: {package} contains Turtle as the authoritative form of the statements, TEI (validated against tei_all) and JSON; every regest page offers its three files separately. Texts and data {ccby}, code {mit}, version {version} of {date}. The sources are {rio} and the {lab}; the source code is on {github}.
